title: Inspiration
definition: Inspiration is the work of God by which the Holy Spirit moved human authors to write the Scriptures so that the words given are truly God's Word, trustworthy and authoritative for faith and practice.
summary: The doctrine of inspiration teaches that Scripture did not originate merely from human will, wisdom, or religious reflection. God worked through real human authors, using their personalities, settings, and language, while ensuring that what was written carried His authority and truth. Because Scripture is inspired by God, it is profitable for teaching, correction, training, and equipping believers for faithful obedience.
christFocus: Inspired Scripture points us to Jesus Christ. The Spirit who inspired the Word glorifies Christ, reveals the truth of Christ, and leads believers to trust in the finished work of Christ. Inspiration matters because through Scripture we are brought to know the Savior and are shaped to follow Him.

studySections.heading: God-Breathed Scripture
studySections.content: Second Timothy 3:16 describes Scripture as breathed out by God. This means Scripture carries divine authority, not because the human writers were impressive, but because God Himself is the ultimate source of His Word.

studySections.heading: Human Authors and Divine Authority
studySections.content: The biblical writers were not treated like machines. God worked through their historical settings, personalities, vocabulary, and experiences, while the Holy Spirit superintended the writing so that the final result was what God intended to say.

studySections.heading: The Purpose of Inspiration
studySections.content: God inspired Scripture so that His people would know truth, be corrected from error, be trained in righteousness, and be equipped for every good work. Inspiration is not merely a doctrine to defend; it is a gift that calls us to hear and obey God.
